title: The last progressive-seeding align calls run one deep query on one thread
body:
In progressive seeding, `seed_progressive` in `nail/src/pipeline/seed_stage.rs` runs `mmseqs align` once per iteration on a slice of the prefilter db. Each iteration doubles `n_take`, the number of candidates a still-active query takes. The active queries shrink to a handful, and the largest slice doubles every iteration.

On the 48-thread box at `bb3c392`, all Pfam against 2,455,940 mgy targets, the last three iterations ran with few cores busy:

| iteration | queries with pairs | largest query slice | wall, s | cpu |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 67 | 51,200 | 2.12 | 1941% |
| 9 | 14 | 102,400 | 2.60 | 833% |
| 10 | 2 | 204,800 | 4.59 | 155% |

Together they took 9.3 s of the 27.1 s align total, in a 205.9 s run. With 48 cores busy the same work would take about 1 s, so the most this could recover is about 8 s, 4% of the run. That bound is arithmetic on the cpu column, not a measurement. The full table and the setup are in a note on nail-e52c52.

The cpu figures fit `mmseqs align` giving each query record of the prefilter db to one thread. Nobody has read the mmseqs source to confirm it.

## Open

- Whether `mmseqs align` accepts one query key in several prefilter records, so nail could split a deep slice into pieces that run on separate threads.
- Whether a cap on `n_take` once few queries remain would change which seeds nail finds. Recall would have to be checked before that trade is made.
- Whether the tail is a fixed shape. At 8 threads on the 16-core box, iteration 11 took 0.34 s, so the shape depends on the thread count and maybe the box.
